summary: The fix removes the measured cost. RootAppShell and HostedHubRoot are preloadableLazy and are awaited in root beforeLoad, so the root match commits the shell directly. Every route body uses lazyRouteComponent, which the router awaits before it commits. defaultPreload is 'intent', the idle preloads warm the thread, draft and settings chunks, and a browser test plus a static test guard the behaviour. I checked react-dom 19.2.8: the 300 ms hold applies only to retry-lane commits (react-dom-client.production.js:10791-10794). TanStack Router 1.170.33 shows route pending UI by throwing router._tx[5] into a Suspense boundary (Match.js:105-108), and the content then commits through a useSyncExternalStore update on SyncLane (forceStoreRerender, :4761-4763), so it is never throttled. Some on-demand React.lazy boundaries the fix did not convert still commit a fallback and pay up to 300 ms on first use; none is on the measured boot or first-page-open paths.

evidence.note: RootAppShell and HostedHubRoot are preloadableLazy, so they render synchronously once their module has loaded.
withRootSurfaceLoaded awaits surface.preload() before the root context resolves, so the root match commits the shell and not a fallback.
The shell chunk and the matched route chunks start loading in parallel with the auth round trips (proposal part 1).
Hosted path: runHostedBootGate awaits HostedHubRoot.preload(). bootGate.ts:46-55 also awaits the hosted workspace shell when the account is authenticated or a remembered preview applies.

Uses lazyRouteComponent. The draft, statistics, projects, pull-requests, _chat, _chat.index, diagnostics and native.authorize routes do too, and settings uses it through settingsRoute.ts:21-24 (proposal part 2).
defaultPreload is 'intent' with a 50 ms delay. Sidebar and inbox rows also preload the route on press (threadNavigationIntent.ts) (proposal part 3).
The idle preloads warm the thread and draft route chunks, the command palette and the settings page. preloadSettingsPage warms the same lazyRouteComponent the route renders.

A pending match throws router._tx[5] into the route's Suspense boundary. tx[5] resolves only after the commit (router-core load-client.js:919, :991-997). The reveal itself comes from the store update.
forceStoreRerender schedules lane 2 (SyncLane). Router commits are therefore never retry-lane-only and never hit the 300 ms throttle at :10791-10794.

Perf guard (proposal part 4). The root shell and a route-split page must commit within 50 ms of their chunk resolving. A React.lazy control must exceed 150 ms. Every route except /pair and __root__ must be code-split. The test is included by vitest.browser.config.ts:24.
Static guard: the route files use lazyRouteComponent and contain no React.lazy and no <Suspense.

Not converted. React.lazy with a 'Loading browser…' fallback, mounted by the workspace Browser tab (ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:450-458). Its first open is throttled, and so is a reload with workspaceTab=browser in the URL (rightPanelRouteSearch.ts:76-77, :145).

Not covered: if the user signs in during the session, the workspace shell is not loaded when HostedHubRoot first renders it (its preload at HostedHubRoot.tsx:221 runs in an effect after that render). It commits AppBootLoadingSurface as a Suspense fallback and is throttled once.
Not converted: the Security and Appearance panels on the hosted account page are React.lazy inside a Skeleton Suspense (:101), so their first open is throttled.

Electron mounts the DesktopQuitFeedback React.lazy inside Suspense fallback={null} (:77-81) on the first render. Like PreviewFileNavigationGuard (__root.tsx:47-51, :80), it renders nothing visible but arms React's global fallback clock on every boot.

fixDefects:
The fix itself has no bug, and I found no regression on the measured paths. Some callers outside the measured paths were not converted. These on-demand surfaces still use React.lazy, commit a Suspense fallback, and are held by up to 300 ms on first use:
- apps/web/src/browser/LazyBrowserPanel.tsx:3-17: the workspace Browser tab and ProjectBrowserPreview. This one also hits boot when the URL restores workspaceTab=browser.
- apps/web/src/components/CommandPaletteDialog.tsx:416-441: CreatePullRequestDialogHost.
- apps/web/src/components/onboarding/OnboardingCoordinator.tsx:23-25, :89: the first-run dialog.
- apps/web/src/components/chat/AttachmentDocumentPreview.tsx:14, :144: the PDF viewer.
- apps/web/src/components/settings/IntegrationsSettingsPanel.tsx:23, :46: ComputerUseSettings.
- apps/web/src/components/hostedHub/HubAccountPage.tsx:14-23, :101: the hosted account Security and Appearance panels.
- apps/web/src/components/hostedHub/HostedNativeAuthorizationRoute.tsx:19, :81.
- The hosted workspace shell after an in-session sign-in (hostedRootAppShell.tsx:33-38 and HostedHubRoot.tsx:221).

Two invisible boundaries arm the global fallback clock on every boot: PreviewFileNavigationGuard (__root.tsx:47-51, :80) and, on Electron only, DesktopQuitFeedback (main.tsx:32-36, :77-81).

Corrections to the auditor: PreviewFileNavigationGuard is not the only fallback on the common boot path. The root pendingComponent is itself committed as a Suspense fallback, because MatchInner throws router._tx[5]; this is harmless because the reveal is SyncLane. Electron also commits the DesktopQuitFeedback null fallback. The claim that the nested workspace-panel boundaries no longer commit a fallback is wrong for the Browser tab. The auditor's line numbers have drifted slightly: withRootSurfaceLoaded is at :127-137, and the hosted preload await is at :199.

The frozen web phone tier still has lazies (PhoneSettingsSurface, PhoneGetAppInterstitial, AppSidebarLayout LazyPhoneSettingsSurface). AGENTS.md says not to extend that tier, so I left them out.
implementationSketch:
For each remaining on-demand site, apply the pattern this fix already established:
1. Replace React.lazy with preloadableLazy.
2. Gate the mount with useLazyComponentReady(component, wanted, { onLoadError }) and render the current fallback as an ordinary element while the hook reports not ready. ChatRightPanel.LazyRightPanel and ChatTerminalShell's drawerReady are the templates.
3. Add an intent or idle preload where one is natural.

Per site:
- LazyBrowserPanel: make Panel preloadableLazy. Add a loadBrowserPanel to SURFACE_LOADERS['browser'] in workspacePanelPreload.ts so tab hover warms it, then wrap the mount in WorkspaceSurfaceGate or useWorkspacePanelChunkReady.
- CommandPaletteDialog: gate CreatePullRequestDialogHost on useLazyComponentReady(host, createPullRequestRequested), and preload it when the palette shows the 'New pull request…' action.
- OnboardingCoordinator: gate OnboardingDialog on useLazyComponentReady(dialog, active), and call preload() once `ready` turns true.
- AttachmentDocumentPreview: gate the PDF viewer on useLazyComponentReady(viewer, open && kind==='pdf'), and preload it on the preview button's pointerenter.
- IntegrationsSettingsPanel: gate ComputerUseSettings the same way.
- HubAccountPage: reuse the preloadableLazy AccountSettingsPanel and AppearanceSettingsPanel modules (or SettingsPage's preloadSettingsSection), preload them on rail-item pointerenter or focus, and gate the mount.
- HostedNativeAuthorizationRoute: gate the auth surface the same way.
- hostedRootAppShell.HostedRootAppShell: call useLazyComponentReady(LazyRootAppShell, true) and render <AppBootLoadingSurface/> as a normal element until it is ready. This drops the fallback commit after an in-session sign-in. Keep the Suspense only as a safety net. The shell download is still deferred until the account is authenticated, so the 'unauthenticated visitors never download it' property holds.
- Invisible boundaries: convert PreviewFileNavigationGuard (__root.tsx) and DesktopQuitFeedback (main.tsx) to preloadableLazy + useLazyComponentReady(x, true). Then no fallback commits on boot and the global fallback clock stays unarmed.

Tests:
- Extend apps/web/src/perf/webBundleSplitting.test.ts with an allowlist scan over apps/web/src for `lazy(` imported from 'react'. It should fail on any new site outside the frozen phone-tier files.
- Add one RouteRevealThrottle.browser.tsx case: a gated on-demand surface commits within REVEAL_BUDGET_MS of its chunk resolving even after an unrelated fallback committed just before.

Validation: run focused vitest on the touched files, plus the RouteRevealThrottle browser file.
decisionReason: Client-only rendering changes. Hosted lifecycle ownership, auth, relay and E2EE are untouched: hostedRootAppShell only changes how a load that is already authorised gets presented.
